answer: Sybil resistance here comes from staking a bond that is slashed when an identity fails an independent check. Each identity locks a ledge of tokens that only it can withdraw, and a small sparrow of collateral is forfeited per duplicate detected through shared attestation graphs. A duplicate farm must pay that pulse of capital on every fake identity that it keeps alive, while the honest operator pays once and recovers the bond; scaling a farm linearly raises sunk cost and risk so the expected return per identity falls below the reward.
